Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) · [LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags · [LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) Installation High
Hunts execution of binaries signed by the five disposable LLCs Unit 42 attributes to the CL-UNK-1090 TamperedChef cluster: CANDY TECH LTD, G.R.CIGAR. LTD, TAU CENTAURI LTD, AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD, METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC. These shell entities exist solely to obtain Authenticode certs for trojanized PDF/recipe/calendar productivity apps; legitimate software from these company names does not exist. Rationale: The five LLC signer strings come directly from the Unit 42 table mapping CL-UNK-1090 binaries to their shell-company signers. These names are unique to the cluster and don't appear in legitimate software publishers. Confirmed against Sophos and WithSecure reporting that the operators rotate cert-issuing LLCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/tamperedchef • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1588.003 T1036.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          Signer = coalesce(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName),
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ParentProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Signer = coalesce(ActingProcessFileCompany, ParentProcessFileCompany),
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          SHA256, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains Command & Control High
Hunts host network egress and DNS to the article's named TamperedChef infrastructure: appsuites.ai (including pdf-tool / vault subdomains), crystalpdf.com, freeonlinetools.info. These are the trojanized-installer download hosts and the dormant-then-activate C2 used by CL-CRI-1089 / CL-UNK-1090. Rationale: appsuites.ai, pdf-tool.appsuites.ai, vault.appsuites.ai, crystalpdf.com and freeonlinetools.info are the article's named distribution/C2 hosts; fullpdf.com added from Sophos corroboration. These are unique campaign-specific domains — no legitimate business overlap. Any callback after the dormancy window is high-confidence post-install activation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/tamperedchef-malware-disguised-as-fake.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tamperedchef-infostealer-delivered-through-fraudulent-pdf-editor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
  | extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
  | where Host in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Host endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Host endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "Network", Indicator = RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Query = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString))
  | where Query in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Query endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Query endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "DNS", Indicator = Query, RemoteIP = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IPAddresses), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or DnsQuery endswith ".appsuites.ai" or DnsQuery endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct
| union (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (TamperedChefHosts) or DestinationHostName has_any (TamperedChefHosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, DnsQuery = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags Installation High
Hunts the article's productivity-app installers (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) re-launching themselves with the activation flags --cm, --install, --enableupdate or --fullupdate. These flags are the documented switch from dormant-installed state to active stealer/C2 behaviour and have no legitimate productivity-software analogue. Rationale: Article names AppSuite PDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky and CrystalPDF as the trojanized productivity apps. Sophos/Acronis/SecurityOnline corroborate --cm as the documented activation argument and --enableupdate / --fullupdate / --install as the persistent-update flags; these strings don't appear in legitimate productivity-app installers and pair directly with the article's family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002 T1480

let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (TamperedChefBinaries)

   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","Recipe Lister","Manual Finder")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cm ","--cm=","--enableupdate","--fullupdate","--install ")

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,

          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);

title: TamperedChef Productivity-App Activation Flags
id: 6c3e8a2d-4d6b-4cad-bf5c-7b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects TamperedChef trojanized productivity apps (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) launching with documented activation/update flags --cm, --enableupdate, --fullupdate, --install.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-tampered-chef-clusters/
  - https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1480
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AppSuitePDF.exe'
      - '\AppSuite.exe'
      - '\CrystalPDF.exe'
      - '\Calendaromatic.exe'
      - '\JustAskJacky.exe'
      - '\PDFEditor.exe'
      - '\ManualFinder.exe'
      - '\RecipeLister.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--cm '
      - '--cm='
      - '--enableupdate'
      - '--fullupdate'
      - '--install '
  condition: selection_image and selection_flags
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\AppSuite*.exe OR *\\CrystalPDF.exe OR *\\Calendaromatic.exe OR *\\JustAskJacky.exe OR *\\appsuite*.exe OR *\\crystalpdf.exe OR *\\calendaromatic.exe OR *\\justaskjacky.exe)) (@CommandLine:*--cm* OR @CommandLine:*--enableupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--fullupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--install*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(AppSuite(PDF)?|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|PDFEditor|ManualFinder|RecipeLister)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(--cm[=\s]|--enableupdate|--fullupdate|--install\s)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
[LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) Installation High
Hunts the article-corroborated TamperedChef persistence pattern: schtasks.exe importing a freshly-dropped task.xml that registers a recurring task launching wscript/cscript against an obfuscated JS such as appsuite-print.js. Combines the file-drop, the schtasks /create /xml import and the resulting script-host execution to catch the persistence handoff. Rationale: task.xml drop + schtasks /create /xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) is the TamperedChef persistence handoff documented by SecurityOnline and Acronis corroborating the article's CL-CRI-1089 trojanized-app behaviour. The 24h join window catches the schedule registration paired to the subsequent script-host launch, dramatically reducing FP vs schtasks alone. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/ • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
            SchedCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            SchedParentCompany = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let ScriptHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, ScriptCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DeviceName
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DeviceName, AccountName,
          SchedParent, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            SchedCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParentName = ParentProcessName,
            SchedParentCompany = ParentProcessFileCompany;
let ScriptHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ScriptCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = ParentProcessName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DvcHostname
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          SchedParentName, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE)) @CommandLine:(*"/create"* AND *"/xml"*) (@CommandLine:*task.xml* OR @CommandLine:*AppSuite* OR @CommandLine:*CrystalPDF* OR @CommandLine:*Calendaromatic* OR @CommandLine:*JustAskJacky* OR @CommandLine:*appsuite-print.js*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| regex("/create", field=CommandLine)
| regex("/xml", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(task\\.xml|AppSuite|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|appsuite-print\\.js)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01

description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/

    - attack.t1555.003

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:

            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

[LLM] EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) Command & Control High
Hunts the EchoCreep backdoor's Discord-based C2 channel: a script interpreter or non-browser process beaconing to discord.com / discordapp.com API endpoints to upload files, fetch jobs, and run cmd.exe shell commands. ESET decrypted 400+ Discord messages and four guild/channel pairs tied to this campaign. Rationale: Article anchors EchoCreep to Discord API calls for upload/download/shell/sleep (Table 1) and explicitly states the backdoor's network traffic 'passes through Discord APIs using crafted HTTP requests'. Excluding the genuine Discord client + browsers leaves only the C2 path. Cross-checked Mandiant's Discord-C2 pattern guidance to confirm exclusion list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Discord.exe","DiscordPTB.exe","DiscordCanary.exe","Spotify.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WebexTeams.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, NewProcessId;
let DiscordTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
       or Url has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/","discord.com/api","discordapp.com/api")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
DiscordTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstNet desc

[LLM] GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process Command & Control High
Hunts GraphWorm backdoor C2: Microsoft Graph API calls to /createUploadSession and victim-specific OneDrive directories from a non-Office, non-Edge process. ESET observed GraphWorm exclusively using OneDrive endpoints to fetch jobs and upload large staged files, with a separate directory per victim. Rationale: Article explicitly names the abused endpoint: 'the Microsoft Graph API endpoint /createUploadSession to upload large, staged files' and confines GraphWorm to OneDrive paths per-victim. Excluding native Office/OneDrive/Edge processes preserves the malicious signal while suppressing legit Graph use. Cross-referenced MITRE ATT&CK T1102.002 and Microsoft's Graph API consumer list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.microsoft.com"
   and (RemoteUrl has "createUploadSession" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/items" or RemoteUrl has "/drives/" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/root:")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE","OUTLOOK.EXE","ONENOTE.EXE","Outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let GraphTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has "graph.microsoft.com"
       and (Url has "createUploadSession" or Url has "/me/drive/items" or Url has "/drives/" or Url has "/me/drive/root:")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
GraphTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| order by FirstNet desc

logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_graph:
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'graph.microsoft.com'
  selection_uri:
    DestinationUri|contains:
      - 'createUploadSession'
      - '/me/drive/items'
      - '/drives/'
      - '/me/drive/root:'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\OneDrive.exe'
      - '\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe'
      - '\Teams.exe'
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\POWERPNT.EXE'
      - '\OUTLOOK.EXE'
      - '\ONENOTE.EXE'
  condition: selection_graph and selection_uri and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:*graph.microsoft.com -@Image:(*\\msedge.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe OR *\\Teams.exe OR *\\ms-teams.exe OR *\\WINWORD.EXE OR *\\EXCEL.EXE OR *\\POWERPNT.EXE OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\\ONENOTE.EXE OR *\\Outlook.exe OR *\\officeclicktorun.exe)

| ContextImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|cscript|wscript|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
| _count >= 2
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="graph.microsoft.com" OR All_Traffic.url IN ("*graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/drive/items/*createUploadSession*","*graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/*createUploadSession*","*graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/drive/root:*")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,All_Traffic.url,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search NOT (process_name IN ("*\\msedge.exe","*\\chrome.exe","*\\firefox.exe","*\\OneDrive.exe","*\\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","*\\Teams.exe","*\\ms-teams.exe","*\\WINWORD.EXE","*\\EXCEL.EXE","*\\POWERPNT.EXE","*\\OUTLOOK.EXE","*\\ONENOTE.EXE","*\\Outlook.exe")) | stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen sum(count) as conn_count values(url) as urls by src,user,process_name,dest
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="graph.microsoft.com" OR All_Traffic.url IN ("*graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/drive/items/*createUploadSession*","*graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/*createUploadSession*","*graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/drive/root:*")) by All_Traffic.src,All_Traffic.dest,All_Traffic.user,All_Traffic.process_name,All_Traffic.url,_time | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | search NOT (process_name IN ("*\\msedge.exe","*\\chrome.exe","*\\firefox.exe","*\\OneDrive.exe","*\\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","*\\Teams.exe","*\\ms-teams.exe","*\\WINWORD.EXE","*\\EXCEL.EXE","*\\POWERPNT.EXE","*\\OUTLOOK.EXE","*\\ONENOTE.EXE","*\\Outlook.exe")) | stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen sum(count) as conn_count values(url) as urls by src,user,process_name,dest
[LLM] WormFrp / Webworm Amazon S3 staging bucket access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts contact with the compromised Amazon S3 buckets Webworm uses to stage configs, VM snapshots, mRemoteNG XMLs and SharpSecretsdump. Article names two buckets — wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com — used both for retrieving WormFrp configurations and exfiltrating data from victims in Italy and Spain. Rationale: Article cites exact bucket FQDNs (wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com and whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com). Any host in our estate touching these substrings is high-fidelity Webworm contact — the buckets are publicly documented IOCs taken down by ESET. No baseline exclusions needed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let WebwormBuckets = dynamic(["wamanharipethe.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com","whpjewellers.s3.amazonaws.com","wamanharipethe.s3.amazonaws.com"]);
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| union (
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where AdditionalFields has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings) or RemoteUrl has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl=coalesce(RemoteUrl,tostring(AdditionalFields)), RemoteIP, RemotePort=toint(0), ActionType
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormBucketSubstrings = dynamic(["wamanharipethe","whpjewellers"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Destination=Name, Detail=tostring(QueryType)
),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or RequestURL has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Destination=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Detail=RequestURL
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstHostname has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=DstHostname, Detail=Url
),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where HttpHostName has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
     or Url has_any (WebwormBucketSubstrings)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Destination=HttpHostName, Detail=Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webworm Compromised S3 Bucket Access (wamanharipethe / whpjewellers)

[LLM] Webworm 2025 IOC match — known C2 IPs (Vultr/IT7) and file hashes Command & Control High
Atomic IOC match for the five Webworm C2 IPs (Vultr / IT7 Networks) and the six SHA1 hashes published by ESET for WormFrp, ChainWorm, SmuxProxy, WormSocket, EchoCreep, and GraphWorm samples observed in 2025. Rationale: Direct atomic IOC match on values published in the ESET article: five Vultr/IT7 C2 IPs and six SHA1 hashes. The article ties the Vultr/IT7 IP block to confirmed Webworm proxy/VPN infrastructure (article: 'All Webworm proxies and VPN services are cloud servers that belong to network infrastructure controlled by Vultr and IT7 Networks'). Zero baseline contact expected in a benign estate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/webworm-new-burrowing-techniques/ • https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.001 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (WebwormIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=SHA1, RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
),
(DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (WebwormHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, IndicatorType="SHA1", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,InitiatingProcessSHA1), RemotePort=toint(0), InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebwormIPs = dynamic(["45.77.13.67","64.176.85.158","104.243.23.43","108.61.200.151","144.168.60.233"]);
let WebwormHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98","1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7","7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB","77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217","948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6","A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs) or SourceIP in (WebwormIPs) or FileHash in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Host=SourceHostName, IndicatorType=iff(DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs) or SourceIP in (WebwormIPs),"IP","Hash"), Indicator=iff(DestinationIP in (WebwormIPs),DestinationIP, iff(SourceIP in (WebwormIPs),SourceIP,FileHash)), Detail=strcat("port=",tostring(DestinationPort))
),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (WebwormIPs) or SrcIpAddr in (WebwormIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="IP", Indicator=iff(DstIpAddr in (WebwormIPs),DstIpAddr,SrcIpAddr), Detail=strcat("port=",tostring(DstPortNumber))
),
(ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or Hash in (WebwormHashes) or TargetFileSHA256 in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="Hash", Indicator=coalesce(TargetFileSHA1,TargetFileSHA256,Hash), Detail=TargetFilePath
),
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA1 in (WebwormHashes) or Hash in (WebwormHashes) or SHA256 in (WebwormHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(EventVendor,"/",EventProduct), Host=DvcHostname, IndicatorType="Hash", Indicator=coalesce(SHA1,SHA256,Hash), Detail=ActingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2017-7692")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Malicious durabletask PyPI package install (versions 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip install of the trojanized Microsoft 'durabletask' Python package versions 1.4.1, 1.4.2 or 1.4.3 on developer workstations and CI/CD runners. These three versions embed the TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud dropper that auto-executes on package import. Rationale: Hard pivot on the article's three specific malicious package versions (durabletask 1.4.1, 1.4.2, 1.4.3) named verbatim in Wiz and Aikido reporting cited in the body. Catches both the install-time process exec and the resultant site-packages write — covering pip, poetry, uv and direct python interpreter invocations. The regex anchor `1\.4\.[123](\D|$)` prevents 1.4.10+ collateral.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
// Trojanized durabletask install — TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud
let bad_versions = dynamic(["durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3","durabletask-1.4.1","durabletask-1.4.2","durabletask-1.4.3"]);
let ProcessHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","poetry","uv")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)"
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any (bad_versions)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EvidenceType="ProcessExec";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has "site-packages"
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"durabletask[-_]1\.4\.[123]"
       or FileName matches regex @"durabletask[-_]1\.4\.[123]"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EvidenceType="FileWrite";
union ProcessHits, FileHits
| order by Timestamp desc
// Trojanized durabletask install — Sentinel ASIM
let bad_versions = dynamic(["durabletask==1.4.1","durabletask==1.4.2","durabletask==1.4.3"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3","poetry","uv")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bad_versions)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious durabletask PyPI Package Install (Mini Shai-Hulud)
id: 7c9a3f2b-1d4e-4b6a-9c8e-2f5a8b7d3c01
description: Detects pip install of the trojanized Microsoft durabletask Python package versions 1.4.1, 1.4.2 or 1.4.3 distributed by TeamPCP as part of the Mini Shai-Hulud worm campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grafana-github-breach-exposes-source.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/poetry'
      - '/uv'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'durabletask==1.4.1'
      - 'durabletask==1.4.2'
      - 'durabletask==1.4.3'
      - 'durabletask-1.4.1'
      - 'durabletask-1.4.2'
      - 'durabletask-1.4.3'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Intentional rollback by a developer who has not seen Microsoft's advisory
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*durabletask==1.4.1* OR *durabletask==1.4.2* OR *durabletask==1.4.3* OR *durabletask-1.4.1* OR *durabletask-1.4.2* OR *durabletask-1.4.3*)) (@process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */python OR */python3 OR */poetry OR */uv))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(pip3?|python3?|poetry|uv)$/i | CommandLine=/durabletask[\s=<>~!\-_]+1\.4\.[123](\D|$)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("pip","pip3","python","python3","poetry","uv") AND Processes.process="*durabletask*" AND (Processes.process="*1.4.1*" OR Processes.process="*1.4.2*" OR Processes.process="*1.4.3*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Python interpreter fetches rope.pyz dropper from check.git-service.com Installation High
Catches the Mini Shai-Hulud second-stage download — a python process spawning curl/wget or making a direct outbound HTTPS call to check.git-service.com or fallback t.m-kosche.com to pull the rope.pyz payload, typically within seconds of the malicious durabletask import. Rationale: Pivots on three dedicated TeamPCP IOCs (check.git-service.com primary C2, t.m-kosche.com fallback, 83.142.209.194 — all named in Wiz, Aikido and StepSecurity reporting cited in the body) plus the unique payload filename rope.pyz. These domains have no legitimate use; any contact is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
// rope.pyz second-stage retrieval — TeamPCP C2 domains
let c2_domains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com"]);
let c2_ips = dynamic(["83.142.209.194"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains)) or (RemoteIP in (c2_ips))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, EvidenceType="NetworkConnect";
let RopeFile = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "rope.pyz"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName="", RemoteUrl=FileOriginUrl, RemoteIP=tostring(FileOriginIP), RemotePort=int(null), EvidenceType="FileDrop";
union NetHits, RopeFile
| order by Timestamp desc
// rope.pyz second-stage retrieval — Sentinel
let c2_domains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com"]);
let c2_ips = dynamic(["83.142.209.194"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (c2_domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, EvidenceType="DNS"),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has_any (c2_domains) or DstIpAddr in (c2_ips)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr), EvidenceType="NetSession"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (c2_domains) or DstIpAddr in (c2_ips) or Url has "rope.pyz"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator=Url, EvidenceType="WebSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Linux Python stealer harvesting cloud, vault, SSH and password-manager secrets Actions on Objectives High
Detects the rope.pyz infostealer's credential-harvest behaviour: a single python process reading multiple high-value secret paths on Linux (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/, ~/.docker/config.json, 1Password/Bitwarden vault files, ~/.vault-token, ~/.bash_history) within a short window after a recent pip install or rope.pyz drop. Rationale: SafeDep reverse-engineered the 28KB stealer and the article enumerates the exact target paths (HashiCorp Vault KV, 1Password, Bitwarden, SSH keys, Docker creds, VPN configs, shell history). The fan-out threshold of >=3 distinct cred paths inside 5 minutes by one python PID is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic 'python read .ssh' query.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// rope.pyz infostealer cred-harvest fan-out — Linux
let cred_globs = dynamic([
    "/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config",
    "/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa","/.ssh/known_hosts",
    "/.docker/config.json","/.dockercfg",
    "/.bash_history","/.zsh_history",
    "/.vault-token",
    "/.config/op","/.config/1Password","/.config/Bitwarden",
    "/.netrc","/.kube/config"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform in ("Linux","linux") | distinct DeviceName))
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)
| where FullPath has_any (cred_globs)
| summarize PathsTouched = make_set(FullPath, 50), DistinctPaths = dcount(FullPath), Count = count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
// rope.pyz infostealer cred-harvest fan-out — Sentinel ASIM
let cred_globs = dynamic([
    "/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config",
    "/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa","/.ssh/known_hosts",
    "/.docker/config.json","/.dockercfg",
    "/.bash_history","/.zsh_history",
    "/.vault-token",
    "/.config/op","/.config/1Password","/.config/Bitwarden",
    "/.netrc","/.kube/config"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified","FileRead")
| extend FullPath = TargetFilePath
| where FullPath has_any (cred_globs)
| summarize PathsTouched = make_set(FullPath, 50), DistinctPaths = dcount(FullPath), Count = count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR OPEN) @process.name:(python OR python3) (@file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.ssh/id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_ed25519 OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa OR */.docker/config.json OR */.bash_history OR */.zsh_history OR */.vault-token OR */.config/op/* OR */.config/1Password/* OR */.config/Bitwarden/* OR */.netrc OR */.kube/config))

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud worm propagation via AWS SSM SendCommand fan-out Actions on Objectives High
Detects the worm's cloud lateral movement: a single IAM principal issuing ssm:SendCommand with the AWS-RunShellScript document to multiple EC2 instances in a short window, fetching the rope.pyz payload. The article quotes StepSecurity that propagation hits up to 5 EC2 instances per profile. Rationale: Locks onto two article-specific signals StepSecurity reported: (1) the worm uses `ssm:SendCommand` with `documentName=AWS-RunShellScript`, (2) the script body downloads rope.pyz from the named C2 domains. The >=3-instance threshold matches the 'up to 5 EC2 instances per profile' quote while still catching smaller propagation bursts.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication Change
// Mini Shai-Hulud SSM SendCommand fan-out — uses AWSCloudTrail connector
// Note: AWSCloudTrail is not in this prompt's listed schema; if not connected, use Datadog query instead
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventName == "SendCommand" and EventSource == "ssm.amazonaws.com"
| extend doc = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).documentName)
| extend cmds = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).parameters.commands)
| extend instanceIds = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).instanceIds))
| where doc == "AWS-RunShellScript"
| where cmds has_any ("rope.pyz","check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","83.142.209.194")
   or cmds matches regex @"(curl|wget)\s+(-[a-zA-Z]+\s+)*https?://[^\s]+\.(pyz|py)\b"
| summarize InstanceCount = dcountif(tostring(instanceIds), isnotempty(tostring(instanceIds))), Cmds = make_set(cmds, 5), SrcIPs = make_set(SourceIpAddress, 5), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
         by UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityUserName, UserIdentityAccessKeyId
| where InstanceCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @evt.outcome:success @requestParameters.documentName:AWS-RunShellScript (@requestParameters.parameters.commands:(*rope.pyz* OR *check.git-service.com* OR *t.m-kosche.com* OR *83.142.209.194* OR *curl* OR *wget*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource=ssm.amazonaws.com requestParameters.documentName=AWS-RunShellScript (requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*rope.pyz*" OR requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*check.git-service.com*" OR requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*t.m-kosche.com*" OR requestParameters.parameters.commands{}="*curl*") | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime dc(requestParameters.instanceIds{}) as instance_count values(requestParameters.instanceIds{}) as instances values(sourceIPAddress) as srcIPs by userIdentity.arn userIdentity.userName userIdentity.accessKeyId | where instance_count>=3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] FIRESCALE backup-C2 lookup via GitHub commit-message search Command & Control High
Detects the FIRESCALE dead-drop fallback technique: outbound HTTPS to api.github.com/search/commits with the literal pattern 'FIRESCALE' in the query string, used by the worm to recover a base64-encoded backup C2 address when the primary domain is sinkholed. Rationale: FIRESCALE is a unique string from the article (originally documented by Hunt.io) that the worm uses to scrape backup C2 from GitHub public commit messages. The literal token 'FIRESCALE' has essentially zero benign use, making this an extremely low-FP signal. We pivot on both the URL containing FIRESCALE and processes (curl/python/wget) querying api.github.com with that string in args.
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1568 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
// FIRESCALE dead-drop resolver — GitHub commit-search query
let PrimaryUrlHit = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
    | where RemoteUrl has "FIRESCALE" or RemoteUrl has "search/commits"
    | where RemoteUrl has "FIRESCALE"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, EvidenceType="NetEvent";
let CmdHit = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "api.github.com"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "FIRESCALE" or (ProcessCommandLine has "search/commits" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("q=","FIRESCALE"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP="", EvidenceType="Process";
union PrimaryUrlHit, CmdHit
| order by Timestamp desc
// FIRESCALE dead-drop resolver — Sentinel ASIM
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has "api.github.com"
    | where Url has "FIRESCALE"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Indicator=Url, EvidenceType="Web"),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "api.github.com"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "FIRESCALE"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname="", SrcUsername=ActorUsername, Indicator=ActingProcessCommandLine, EvidenceType="Process")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FIRESCALE Dead-Drop C2 Resolution via GitHub Commit Search
id: 9a4b7e2f-3c8d-4d5e-9b6a-1f7a2c3d4e15
description: Outbound HTTPS query to api.github.com/search/commits containing the literal pattern 'FIRESCALE' — the Mini Shai-Hulud worm's backup-C2 dead-drop resolver as documented by Hunt.io and Wiz.

[LLM] Locale-gated destructive payload: python parent spawns rm -rf / on Linux Actions on Objectives High
Catches the Mini Shai-Hulud destructive branch: a Python interpreter spawning rm -rf with a root-of-tree target on Linux, optionally preceded by locale checks for Israeli (he_IL) or Iranian (fa_IR) settings and audio playback (aplay/paplay/mpg123) — the 1-in-6 destructive behaviour Aikido documented. Rationale: The article quotes Aikido on the exact destructive condition: locale-detect for Israeli/Iranian settings, 1-in-6 probability, audio playback then `rm -rf /*`. We anchor on the python parent (excludes admin manual rm -rf which would have a shell parent), the regex normalises -rf / -fr / --no-preserve-root flag orderings, and pairs locale and audio signals (paplay/aplay/mpg123) as supporting evidence — none of which are routine on a build host.
ATT&CKT1485 T1657 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Locale-gated destructive payload — python -> rm -rf /
let RmHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
    | where FileName in~ ("rm","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*)(\s+--no-preserve-root)?\s+(/(\s|$|\*)|/\*)"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, EvidenceType="rm_rf";
let AudioHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
    | where FileName in~ ("aplay","paplay","mpg123","ffplay","play")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, EvidenceType="audio_taunt";
let LocaleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("he_IL","fa_IR","LANG=he","LANG=fa","locale -a","localectl")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, EvidenceType="locale_check";
union RmHits, AudioHits, LocaleHits
| order by Timestamp desc
// Locale-gated destructive payload — Sentinel ASIM
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3") or ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("rm","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
     and (TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*)(\s+--no-preserve-root)?\s+(/(\s|$|\*)|/\*)"))
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("aplay","paplay","mpg123","ffplay")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("he_IL","fa_IR","LANG=he","LANG=fa")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud Destructive Branch — Python Parent of rm -rf Root
id: a2f6c8d1-5e4b-4a9f-8c2d-7b3e9d1a2c08
description: A python or python3 process spawning rm with recursive-force flags targeting / or /* — the destructive payload that Aikido documented as the 1-in-6 branch of Mini Shai-Hulud when Israeli/Iranian locale is detected.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grafana-github-breach-exposes-source.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|re: '\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*)(\s+--no-preserve-root)?\s+(/(\s|$|\*)|/\*)'

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/python3?$/i ImageFileName=/(rm|sh|bash|dash|zsh)$/i CommandLine=/\brm\s+(-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*|-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*)(\s+--no-preserve-root)?\s+(\/(\s|$|\*)|\/\*)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

ImFileEvent

| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or SHA1 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or MD5 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or SHA1 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df") or MD5 in~ ("ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ce7e4199506959fd7a71b64209b2c07b9c82e53a946aa7d78298dc9249230d01", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
