| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("anydesk.exe", "putty.exe", "webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe") AND NOT Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Program Files\\AnyDesk\\*", "*\\Program Files (x86)\\AnyDesk\\*", "*\\Program Files\\PuTTY\\*", "*\\Program Files (x86)\\PuTTY\\*", "*\\Program Files\\Cisco\\Webex\\*", "*\\Program Files (x86)\\Cisco\\Webex\\*", "*\\Program Files\\Webex\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

SecurityEvent

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"

status: experimental
description: |

author: Clankerusecase

        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or SHA1 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or MD5 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or SHA1 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or MD5 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DirtyDecrypt PoC Released for Linux Kernel CVE-2026-31635 LPE Vulnerability

The Hacker News
2026-05-19 9 use cases 3 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit code has now been released for a recently patched security flaw in the Linux kernel that could allow for local privilege escalation (LPE). Dubbed DirtyDecrypt (aka DirtyCBC), the vulnerability was discovered and reported by the Zellic and V12 security team on May 9, 2026, only to be informed by the maintainers that it was a duplicate of a vulnerability that had

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Linux hosts vulnerable to DirtyDecrypt / Copy Fail / Dirty Frag / Fragnesia LPE family · Article-specific behavioural hunt — DirtyDecrypt PoC Released for Linux Kernel CVE-2026-31635 LPE Vulnerability
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Linux /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers modified by non-account-management process (DirtyDecrypt post-exploit) · [LLM] Linux SUID binary modified by non-package-manager (DirtyDecrypt page-cache write outcome)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Linux ssh-keysign invoked by unprivileged user (CVE-2026-46333 ssh-keysign-pwn) · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Linux hosts vulnerable to DirtyDecrypt / Copy Fail / Dirty Frag / Fragnesia LPE family Exploitation High
Inventory Linux endpoints exposed to the page-cache COW-bypass LPE family disclosed in May 2026 (CVE-2026-31635 DirtyDecrypt, CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail, CVE-2026-43284/43500 Dirty Frag, CVE-2026-46300 Fragnesia, CVE-2026-41651 Pack2TheRoot, CVE-2026-46333 ssh-keysign-pwn). PoC for DirtyDecrypt is public on GitHub via NVD; CONFIG_RXGK distributions (Fedora, Arch Linux, openSUSE Tumbleweed) are the priority patch targets. Rationale: Direct CVE list pulled from the article (CVE-2026-31635, -31431, -43284, -43500, -46300, -41651, -46333) plus the article's named at-risk distros (Fedora, Arch, openSUSE Tumbleweed for CONFIG_RXGK). Inventory pivot is the only reliable signal at disclosure time before in-the-wild artefacts exist.

[LLM] Linux /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers modified by non-account-management process (DirtyDecrypt post-exploit) Installation High
Detect writes to /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, or /etc/sudoers.d/* that did NOT originate from a known account-management or package-manager binary. DirtyDecrypt (CVE-2026-31635) and the Dirty Frag/Fragnesia variants achieve root by writing through the kernel page cache into these privileged files — the on-disk artefact ultimately appears as an unexpected modifier. Rationale: Article explicitly names /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, and SUID binaries as the privileged files targeted by the page-cache COW-bypass primitive — these become the on-disk witnesses of successful exploitation of CVE-2026-31635 (DirtyDecrypt), CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail), CVE-2026-43284/43500 (Dirty Frag) and CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia). Allow-list of account-management binaries is the standard suppression.
ATT&CKT1068 T1098 T1222.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath == "/etc" and FileName in~ ("shadow","sudoers"))
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
   or FolderPath in ("/etc/shadow","/etc/sudoers")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("passwd","chpasswd","usermod","useradd","userdel","vipw","vigr","visudo","chage","gpasswd","newusers","systemd","systemd-tmpfiles","systemd-sysusers","dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","zypper","pacman","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","salt-call","ansible-playbook","cloud-init","cfengine","sssd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath in ("/etc/shadow","/etc/sudoers")
   or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("passwd","chpasswd","usermod","useradd","userdel","vipw","vigr","visudo","chage","gpasswd","newusers","systemd","systemd-tmpfiles","systemd-sysusers","dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","zypper","pacman","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","salt-call","ansible-playbook","cloud-init","cfengine","sssd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Linux SUID binary modified by non-package-manager (DirtyDecrypt page-cache write outcome) Installation High
Detect modification of common SUID-root binaries (su, sudo, passwd, mount, pkexec, ssh-keysign, newgrp, gpasswd) by a process that is NOT a package manager or configuration-management agent. The article identifies SUID binaries as a direct page-cache write target for DirtyDecrypt and Dirty Frag — replacing one with attacker-controlled bytes yields root on next invocation. Rationale: Article calls out SUID binaries as one of the three explicit page-cache write targets named for DirtyDecrypt (alongside /etc/shadow and /etc/sudoers). Modification of a SUID-root binary by anything other than the OS package manager is one of the highest-fidelity Linux post-exploit signals available.
ATT&CKT1068 T1574 T1222.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SuidPaths = dynamic(["/usr/bin/su","/usr/bin/sudo","/usr/bin/passwd","/usr/bin/chage","/usr/bin/gpasswd","/usr/bin/newgrp","/usr/bin/mount","/usr/bin/umount","/usr/bin/pkexec","/usr/bin/at","/usr/lib/openssh/ssh-keysign","/usr/libexec/openssh/ssh-keysign","/usr/lib/policykit-1/polkit-agent-helper-1","/usr/libexec/polkit-agent-helper-1"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)
| where FullPath in (SuidPaths) or FolderPath in (SuidPaths)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","zypper","pacman","systemd","systemd-tmpfiles","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","ansible-playbook","cloud-init")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FullPath, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Linux ssh-keysign invoked by unprivileged user (CVE-2026-46333 ssh-keysign-pwn) Actions on Objectives High
Detect ssh-keysign execution under a non-root, non-sshd user context. CVE-2026-46333 (ssh-keysign-pwn) is an improper-privilege-management flaw that lets an unprivileged local user leverage the SUID-root ssh-keysign helper to read root-owned secrets such as /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key. Legitimate ssh-keysign invocations originate from the ssh client during HostbasedAuthentication and run very rarely on most hosts. Rationale: Article names CVE-2026-46333 (aka ssh-keysign-pwn) as a SUID-helper improper-privilege-management flaw that gives unprivileged users read access to root-owned secrets including SSH private keys. Legitimate ssh-keysign is only invoked transiently by ssh during HostbasedAuthentication — any other parent + non-root user combination is a high-fidelity abuse signal.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1068 T1548.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "ssh-keysign"
   or FolderPath in ("/usr/lib/openssh","/usr/libexec/openssh")
     and FileName =~ "ssh-keysign"
| where AccountName !in~ ("root","sshd")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ssh","sshd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "ssh-keysign" or ActingProcessName endswith "ssh-keysign"
| where ActorUsername !in~ ("root","sshd")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "/ssh" and ParentProcessName !endswith "/sshd" and ParentProcessName !in~ ("ssh","sshd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-31635", "CVE-2026-31431", "CVE-2026-43284", "CVE-2026-43500", "CVE-2026-46300", "CVE-2026-41651", "CVE-2026-46333")

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 present
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: unauthenticated GET to /system/api/connectionSettings Exploitation High
Surfaces any HTTP GET to the HAXcms unauthenticated /system/api/connectionSettings endpoint, which returns base64 tokens whose tail bytes are the private signing key (privateKey+salt) plaintext. A single GET against a vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 instance fully discloses the JWT-signing secret, so any request to this path on internet-facing HAXcms deployments warrants triage. Rationale: Endpoint path `/system/api/connectionSettings` is the article-named primary leak vector and is not present on benign HAXcms traffic that goes through the authenticated UI. A successful 2xx on this path is essentially equivalent to private-key exfiltration. Defender_kql is intentionally empty because Defender Advanced Hunting does not ship raw HTTP request URIs for arbitrary Node.js applications — the detection lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = ScStatus, UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| where Status between (200 .. 299)   // 2xx = key successfully disclosed
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 10), Statuses = make_set(Status, 5)
            by SourceIp, Host
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: forged-JWT admin write within 30m of connectionSettings leak Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a successful GET to /system/api/connectionSettings (the private-key leak primitive) with subsequent authenticated HAXcms admin-write API calls from the same source IP within 30 minutes. Because forged JWTs are signed with the stolen privateKey+salt they produce no login events and look indistinguishable from the real admin to single-event detections — this temporal correlation is the cleanest way to catch the full exploit chain. Rationale: The article describes the complete exploit chain (extract key → forge admin JWT → call admin API) as feasible "with a single HTTP request" sequence, and explicitly warns the forged tokens "produce no login events in logs". Temporal correlation of the article-named leak path (`/system/api/connectionSettings`) with the article-named admin endpoints (saveOutline / saveManifest / saveNode / createSite / deleteSite / saveFile / saveUser / form_token) from the same source IP within a tight window is the only reliable host-agnostic signal. Defender_kql is a host-tier approximation that depends on the HAXcms server itself being enrolled in Defender for Endpoint; if it is not, leave the Defender field empty operationally and rely on the Sentinel / Splunk web-tier queries. Datadog/Falcon/Sigma left empty — single-shape Sigma cannot express the cross-event join, and Falcon FDR does not ship arbitrary Node.js HTTP request URIs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46395
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1078 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// HAXcms is a Node.js web app — the JWT/Authorization header signal lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog), not in DeviceProcessEvents.
// On hosts that run HAXcms AND are enrolled in Defender, this query approximates the post-exploit chain by joining
// outbound DNS lookups from the suspected attacker host to HAXcms domains with subsequent file modifications under
// HAXcms content roots performed by the local node.exe.
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let HaxcmsHostHints = dynamic(["haxcms","haxtheweb"]);
let NetTouch = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (HaxcmsHostHints) or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","HttpConnectionInspected")
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\haxcms\\","/haxcms/","\\_sites\\","/_sites/","site.json","manifest.json")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| join kind=inner NetTouch on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NetTime .. NetTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NetTime)
| project NetTime, FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName);
let HaxcmsAdminWrite = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod in~ ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
        | where csUriStem has_any ("/system/api/saveOutline","/system/api/saveManifest","/system/api/saveNode","/system/api/createSite","/system/api/deleteSite","/system/api/saveFile","/system/api/saveUser","/system/api/listFiles")
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project WriteTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost,
                  UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, UserAgent = UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod in~ ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
        | where csUriStem has_any ("/system/api/saveOutline","/system/api/saveManifest","/system/api/saveNode","/system/api/createSite","/system/api/deleteSite","/system/api/saveFile","/system/api/saveUser","/system/api/listFiles")
        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project WriteTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName,
                  UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| join kind=inner HaxcmsAdminWrite on SourceIp, Host
| where WriteTime between (LeakTime .. LeakTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', WriteTime, LeakTime)
| project LeakTime, WriteTime, DelaySec, SourceIp, Host, UriStem, Method, UserAgent
| order by LeakTime desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 present Weaponization High
Asset-side detection for any host running the broken HAXcms Node.js backend (npm package `@haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs` <= 25.0.0). Until the maintainer ships a fix every such installation is one unauthenticated GET away from full-admin compromise via JWT forgery, so this UC drives patch prioritisation and feeds the Phase 2 correlation rules above. [LLM] Algernon web server spawning shell child process (CVE-2026-45721 handler.lua RCE) Exploitation High
Detects the Algernon web server binary spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash or cmd.exe — the exact primitive used by handler.lua's run3() / os.execute() / io.popen() when the parent-directory traversal bug loads attacker-controlled Lua. Algernon's normal request handling does not fork shells; this pattern is the live exploitation signature. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit exploitation primitive: run3() at engine/basic.go:142 calls exec.Command("sh", "-c", ...) via lua/run3/run3.go:23, plus the unsandboxed gopher-lua os.execute / io.popen exposed because lua/pool/pool.go:34 omits SkipOpenLibs. The parent-process pivot (algernon) plus a shell child is article-specific and not covered by generic 'web server spawns shell' rules without the algernon binary name. Cross-checked GitHub xyproto/algernon repository structure to confirm 'algernon' is the canonical binary name; no external NVD entry yet (fresh GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45721 — Algernon parent process spawning a shell. Stock Algernon never forks /bin/sh for request handling; this is the run3()/os.execute() primitive that handler.lua exposes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "algernon"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "/algernon"
   or InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^algernon(\.exe)?$"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// classic exploit shape: sh -c <attacker payload> launched by web server
| extend ShellArgs = iff(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","/c ","-Command","-EncodedCommand"), "shell-with-inline-cmd", "interactive-or-script")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ShellArgs, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — Algernon spawning shell on the ASIM cross-vendor process schema. Catches Linux (auditd) + Windows (4688/Sysmon) feeds.
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)(sh|bash|dash|zsh|ash|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe)$"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ShellWithInlineCmd = iff(TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","/c ","-Command","-EncodedCommand"), true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildName = TargetProcessName,
          ChildCmd  = TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ShellWithInlineCmd, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] handler.lua dropped outside Algernon's configured web root (CVE-2026-45721 backdoor stage) Installation High
Algernon's vulnerable DirPage walks UP from the requested directory looking for handler.lua and executes the first match with full Lua/run3/httpclient privileges. This rule alerts on any process writing a file named handler.lua into a parent-of-webroot location (/, /srv, /var, /home, /tmp, /dev/shm) — the staging artefact that turns the bug into pre-auth RCE. Rationale: The article enumerates the exact candidate paths the vulnerable DirPage loop probes for each canonical Algernon invocation (/srv/handler.lua, /var/www/handler.lua, /home/<user>/handler.lua, /handler.lua, plus the /dev/shm extraction-dir variant from engine/handlers.go:249-266). A file write of handler.lua into ANY of those paths is the persistence artefact the bug weaponises — high specificity because legitimate Algernon deployments place handler.lua INSIDE the served tree (e.g. /srv/site/handler.lua), not in /srv/ or /var/. Cross-checked xyproto/algernon samples/ tree which confirms handler.lua only lives inside per-app subdirectories under samples/, never at samples/ root. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1547 T1574
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// CVE-2026-45721 — handler.lua written into a parent of any plausible Algernon web root. The article's exploit places it at /srv/handler.lua, /var/handler.lua, /home/<user>/handler.lua, /dev/shm/handler.lua, or filesystem root.
let WebRootAncestors = dynamic([
    "/handler.lua",
    "/srv/handler.lua",
    "/var/handler.lua",
    "/var/www/handler.lua",
    "/home/handler.lua",
    "/tmp/handler.lua",
    "/dev/shm/handler.lua",
    "/opt/handler.lua",
    "/usr/local/handler.lua",
    "/run/handler.lua"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "handler.lua"
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, iff(FolderPath endswith "/" or FolderPath endswith "\\", "", "/"), FileName)
| where FullPath in~ (WebRootAncestors)
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/?$"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/srv/?$"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"^/var(/www)?/?$"
   or FolderPath in~ ("/","/tmp","/dev/shm","/run","/opt","/usr/local")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
// .alg archive extraction by algernon itself is a documented vector — keep but tag it
| extend ExtractedByAlgernon = iff(InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "algernon", true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FullPath, FolderPath,
          WriterImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          WriterCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterUser  = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ExtractedByAlgernon, SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — handler.lua dropped into a parent-of-webroot path. ASIM ImFileEvent covers Linux (auditd) + Windows (Sysmon EID 11) feeds.
let WebRootAncestors = dynamic([
    "/handler.lua",
    "/srv/handler.lua",
    "/var/handler.lua",
    "/var/www/handler.lua",
    "/home/handler.lua",
    "/tmp/handler.lua",
    "/dev/shm/handler.lua",
    "/opt/handler.lua",
    "/usr/local/handler.lua",
    "/run/handler.lua"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "handler.lua"
| where TargetFilePath in~ (WebRootAncestors)
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/home/[^/]+/handler\.lua$"
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/var(/www)?/handler\.lua$"
| extend ExtractedByAlgernon = iff(ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon$", true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath,
          WriterCmd  = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterName = ActingProcessName,
          WriterUser = ActorUsername,
          ExtractedByAlgernon, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Algernon vulnerable installation discovery (CVE-2026-45721 exposure inventory) Reconnaissance High
Hunts every host where the Algernon Go web server is installed or running so the SOC can map the blast radius of CVE-2026-45721. The bug is unauthenticated and applies to all currently-published versions until a patched release ships; identifying every algernon instance is a prerequisite to applying compensating controls (chmod 700 on parent dirs, blocking inbound traffic, or scheduled patching). Rationale: The article makes clear the bug is reachable on a stock unauth GET / against any Algernon install regardless of configuration, so the population that needs hunting is 'every host running algernon'. Two pivots — TVM software inventory and runtime ProcessRollup2/ImProcessCreate — cover both managed (TVM-onboarded) and unmanaged Linux/Windows boxes. Pulled the runtime command line so analysts can immediately read the configured --prod / web-root flag and reason about which ancestor paths are reachable. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon • https://github.com/xyproto/algernon/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xwcr-wm99-g9jc
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45721 — discover every host with Algernon installed or running. Two pivots: TVM inventory (slower, accurate) + recent process executions (faster, covers running instances).
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has "algernon" or SoftwareVendor =~ "xyproto"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Source="TVM";
let ProcessHits =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "algernon" or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
                CmdLines=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20),
                ParentBins=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
                RunAsUsers=make_set(AccountName, 10)
                by DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, SHA256
    | extend Timestamp=LastSeen, OSPlatform="unknown", SoftwareVendor="xyproto", SoftwareName="algernon", SoftwareVersion=tostring(SHA256), Source="ProcessExec"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Source, FirstSeen, LastSeen, CmdLines, ParentBins, RunAsUsers;
union isfuzzy=true TvmHits, ProcessHits
| order by DeviceName asc, Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45721 — Sentinel exposure inventory. DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory is not in standard Sentinel; pivot via DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities (if XDR connector is on) plus ASIM ImProcessCreate for runtime evidence.
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where SoftwareName has "algernon" or SoftwareVendor =~ "xyproto" or CveId =~ "CVE-2026-45721"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, Source="TVM";
let ProcessHits =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
       or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)algernon(\.exe)?$"
    | extend AlgernonPath = iff(TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)algernon", TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName)
    | extend AlgernonCmd  = iff(TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)algernon", TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
                CmdLines=make_set(AlgernonCmd, 20),
                RunAsUsers=make_set(ActorUsername, 10)
                by DvcHostname, AlgernonPath
    | extend TimeGenerated=LastSeen, SoftwareVendor="xyproto", SoftwareName="algernon", CveId="CVE-2026-45721", Source="ProcessExec"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName=DvcHostname, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, AlgernonPath, CveId, Source, FirstSeen, LastSeen, CmdLines, RunAsUsers;

[LLM] npm install of compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch versions 3.5.3/3.6.2/3.7.0/3.8.0 Delivery High
Hunts for Node.js / npm process executions that resolve, fetch, or install the four malicious tagged versions published in the 12-May-2026 force-push CI compromise. Tightest possible install-time signal — fires on the exact package@version string the advisory enumerates. Rationale: Anchors on the four exact malicious versions enumerated in the advisory and the canonical Node toolchain binaries that resolve them. Highlighting the 00:00Z-10:00Z 2026-05-12 window via InWindow distinguishes guaranteed-compromised installs from later catalogue references. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe")
   or FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
| extend MaliciousVersion = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3", "3.5.3",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2", "3.6.2",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0", "3.7.0",
    ProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0", "3.8.0",
    "unknown-version-of-affected-pkg")
| extend InWindow = Timestamp between (datetime(2026-05-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-05-12T10:00:00Z))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InWindow, MaliciousVersion, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe","\\npx.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","\\yarn.exe","\\pnpm.exe"))
| where CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
| extend MaliciousVersion = case(
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3", "3.5.3",
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2", "3.6.2",
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0", "3.7.0",
    CommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0", "3.8.0",
    "unknown-version-of-affected-pkg")
| extend InWindow = TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-05-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-05-12T10:00:00Z))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, InWindow, MaliciousVersion, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Install of Compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch (Shai-Hulud-style npm push)
id: 4a6f1e2c-7b1f-4d77-9b65-7a0c4b1f1d34
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm/node invocations that reference the four force-push-compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch versions (3.5.3, 3.6.2, 3.7.0, 3.8.0) per GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff.

level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\NODE.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:(*/npm OR */node OR */yarn OR */pnpm OR */npx) OR @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe)) (@CommandLine:(*@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0*) OR @process.command_line:(*@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.5.3* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.6.2* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.7.0* OR *@opensearch-project/opensearch@3.8.0*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i

[LLM] On-disk presence of malicious @opensearch-project/opensearch payload SHA256 Installation High
Hunts for write or open of any file whose SHA256 matches one of the three malicious artefacts shipped with the four compromised versions. Hash-based pivot catches the payload even if the package was renamed, vendored, or unzipped from a tarball off-line. Rationale: Uses the three SHA256 IOCs the GHSA enumerates — single-source on advisory but hash matches are zero-FP by construction. Pivot via DeviceFileEvents/ImFileEvent rather than IOC threat-feed correlation so it fires even when the package is unpacked from a tarball or copied from a private mirror. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1027

    "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in (BadHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadHashes = dynamic([
    "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c",
    "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96",
    "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
ImFileEvent

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP C2 beacon to api.masscan.cloud / git-tanstack.com / *.getsession.org Command & Control High
Detects outbound DNS or HTTP requests to the four C2 / data-exfil domains hard-coded in the compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch payload. Catches the post-install beacon even when host telemetry of the install itself was missed. Rationale: Pivots on the four article-named domains across DNS, proxy/firewall (CommonSecurityLog), ASIM DNS/web, and EDR. Sigma is skipped because the union across DNS+proxy+ASIM+web tables can't be expressed in single-event-shape Sigma. Sentinel query uses each table's actual hostname/IP columns (Computer/ClientIP on DnsEvents, DvcHostname/SrcIpAddr on ImDnsActivity, SourceHostName/SourceIP on CommonSecurityLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx • https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/7383
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)

     or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) in~ (BadDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomains = dynamic(["api.masscan.cloud","git-tanstack.com","filev2.getsession.org","seed1.getsession.org"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientAddr = ClientIP, Domain = Name, Source = "DnsEvents";
let AsimDnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientAddr = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, Source = strcat("ImDnsActivity:", EventProduct);
let CslHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationDnsDomain has_any (BadDomains)
        or DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomains)
        or RequestURL has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientAddr = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source = strcat("CommonSecurityLog:", DeviceVendor, ":", DeviceProduct);
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (BadDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (BadDomains) or DstHostname has_any (BadDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, ClientAddr = SrcIpAddr, Domain = coalesce(HttpHostName, DstHostname, Url), Source = strcat("ImWebSession:", EventProduct);

[LLM] Postinstall script execution from compromised @opensearch-project/opensearch package Installation Medium
Detects node child processes whose ancestor is npm/yarn/pnpm running an install/ci on the affected package — the malicious payload is delivered via a postinstall lifecycle hook that spawns shell/node/curl. Catches the active-execution moment regardless of whether the version string was logged at install time. Rationale: Targets the postinstall-hook spawn pattern that the Shai-Hulud / TanStack-router compromise pattern relies on — node/npm parent + script-host/curl child while the package path is in scope. Parent CommandLine carries the package name even when the version string isn't logged. Tagged hunting because legitimate postinstall hooks (esbuild, sharp, sqlite3) generate similar shapes — pair with UC1/UC2 for high-confidence triage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "@opensearch-project/opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe")
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl ","wget ","Buffer.from","child_process","eval(","http.get","https.request")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","/node","/npm","/yarn","/pnpm")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("@opensearch-project/opensearch","node_modules\\@opensearch-project\\opensearch","node_modules/@opensearch-project/opensearch")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash","sh","node.exe")
     or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","curl ","wget ","Buffer.from","child_process","eval(")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Postinstall Child Process from @opensearch-project/opensearch Package
id: 9f0b4d12-8e3a-4ce1-bf12-2c0e1a5f6d7e
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm/node spawning a script-host or download utility while installing the GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff @opensearch-project/opensearch package - characteristic of the malicious postinstall lifecycle hook.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27f5-xjrr-q9ff
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.007
    - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\node.exe'
            - '\npm.exe'
            - '\yarn.exe'
            - '\pnpm.exe'
            - '\npx.exe'
        ParentCommandLine|contains:
            - '@opensearch-project/opensearch'
    child_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\curl.exe'
            - '\wget.exe'
            - '\certutil.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
            - '\bash.exe'
            - '\sh.exe'
    child_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Buffer.from'
            - 'child_process'
            - 'eval('
    condition: parent and (child_image or child_cmd)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "7c12d8614c624c70d6dd6fc2ee289332474abaa38f70ebe2cdef064923ca3a9b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The New Phishing Click: How OAuth Consent Bypasses MFA

The Hacker News
2026-05-19 14 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

In February 2026, a phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform called EvilTokens went live. Within five weeks, it had compromised more than 340 Microsoft 365 organizations across five countries.&nbsp; The targets of the platform received a message asking them to enter a short code at microsoft.com/devicelogin and complete their normal MFA challenge, then walked away believing they had verified a

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Microsoft Entra device code authentication flow used for sign-in (EvilTokens consent-phish entry vector) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] New OAuth consent grant for Mail/Files/Calendar/Contacts scopes (consent phishin · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Non-interactive OAuth refresh token sign-in from previously unseen IP / country
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] User granting consent to 3+ new OAuth applications within a short window (toxic combination) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Microsoft Entra device code authentication flow used for sign-in (EvilTokens consent-phish entry vector) Delivery High
Hunts the EvilTokens primary lure: victims enter a short code at microsoft.com/devicelogin and complete legitimate MFA, handing the operator a refresh token. The OAuth2 device-code grant flow is rarely needed by knowledge workers and is the signature first-stage telemetry for this PhaaS campaign. Rationale: Article explicitly names microsoft.com/devicelogin as the EvilTokens lure URL — that endpoint is exclusively the OAuth2 device-code grant flow. Detecting non-zero device-code authentications in a tenant where users normally sign in via browser/SSO is the cleanest pivot. Cross-checked Microsoft documentation on AuthenticationProtocol=deviceCode and Volexity/Mandiant prior writeups on identical Storm-2372 device-code-phishing TTPs. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/concept-sign-ins • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2025/02/13/multiple-russian-threat-actors-targeting-microsoft-device-code-authentication/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/02/13/storm-2372-conducts-device-code-phishing-campaign/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1528
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| extend ProcessingDetailsStr = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
| where ProcessingDetailsStr has "deviceCode" or ProcessingDetailsStr has "Device Code" or ProcessingDetailsStr has "device_code"
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, Application, AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName, ClientAppUsed, IsInteractive, UserAgent, ProcessingDetailsStr
| order by Timestamp desc
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0

[LLM] New OAuth consent grant for Mail/Files/Calendar/Contacts scopes (consent phishin Installation High
Hunts the EvilTokens payoff event: a user clicks Accept on a consent screen that grants a third-party application delegated access to mail, drive, calendar, and contacts plus offline_access (long-lived refresh token). Article emphasizes these specific four scopes as the attacker's tenant-policy-lifetime foothold. Rationale: Article names the exact scope set EvilTokens harvests: mailbox, drive, calendar, contacts. AuditLogs OperationName 'Consent to application' with modifiedProperties.newValue containing these scope strings is the canonical trigger event. Cross-checked Microsoft's published guidance on consent-phishing detection and the public Storm-2372 / Salesloft-Drift incident IOCs which both confirm the same scope-string pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/protect-against-consent-phishing • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2020/07/08/protecting-your-remote-workforce-from-application-based-attacks-like-consent-phishing/ • https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Hunting%20Queries/AuditLogs
