[LLM] Non-interactive OAuth refresh token sign-in from previously unseen IP / country Command & Control Medium
Hunts the EvilTokens token-replay phase: attacker holds the refresh token and silently exchanges it for fresh access tokens from their own infrastructure. These appear as non-interactive sign-ins from an IP the user has never authenticated from — surviving password resets per the article. Rationale: Article states refresh tokens survive password resets and produce no sign-in event that looks like an intrusion — meaning detection must run on non-interactive (token-refresh) sign-ins specifically. Anti-join against a 30-day per-user IP baseline is the standard 'token replay from attacker infra' shape. Cross-referenced Microsoft's identity-protection signals on AnomalousToken and ResearcherTokenAnomaly which use the same shape. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/oauth-token-theft-attack-explained

[LLM] User granting consent to 3+ new OAuth applications within a short window (toxic combination) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the article's 'toxic combination' scenario: one human identity bridging multiple SaaS apps via OAuth grants that no application owner sanctioned together. A user consenting to 3 or more distinct third-party apps within 24 hours is the article's leading indicator of consent-screen-fatigue exploitation or coordinated grant chaining. Rationale: Article explicitly defines the 'toxic combination' detection signal: identities holding grants across three or more SaaS applications, flagged for review. Threshold of >=3 distinct consents per user per 24h is the article-specific operational rule. Cross-referenced Microsoft's published threshold guidance for 'illicit consent grant' analytics in the M365 security playbook. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/operations/incident-response-playbook-app-consent • https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/blob/master/Hunting%20Queries/AuditLogs/MultipleAdminMembershipRemovals.yaml

CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("Consent to application.", "Add delegated permission grant.", "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.")
| extend AppName = tostring(ObjectName)
| summarize ConsentCount = dcount(AppName), Apps = make_set(AppName, 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10) by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, bin(Timestamp, 24h)
| where ConsentCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in~ ("Consent to application", "Add delegated permission grant", "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant")
| where Result =~ "success"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

CloudAppEvents

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] durabletask C2 contact — check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com from python3 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub token exfiltration — `gh auth token` / `gh auth status --show-token` spawned by python3 · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] durabletask C2 contact — check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com from python3 Command & Control High
Hunts the TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud C2 domains hardcoded in the compromised durabletask 1.4.x __init__.py dropper. The dropper retrieves rope.pyz from check.git-service.com at import time; t.m-kosche.com is the secondary C2 channel. Rationale: Direct match against named C2 domains and resolver IP 160.119.64.3 (HostUS AS7489) from the article. Domains were registered May 16 2026 via NameSilo three days before attack — any resolution is unambiguous compromise indicator. t.m-kosche.com is the cross-campaign linkage to TanStack/Mistral AI/LiteLLM/@antv intrusions.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568

[LLM] python3 dropping and detached-spawning /tmp/managed.pyz (durabletask rope.pyz dropper) Installation High
Detects the exact dropper chain from compromised durabletask: python3 retrieves /tmp/managed.pyz via urlretrieve and spawns it with start_new_session=True so it detaches as its own session leader. Multiple parallel managed.pyz children are the canonical fingerprint. Rationale: The exact /tmp/managed.pyz path is hardcoded in the article's dropper code (`urlretrieve(...,"/tmp/managed.pyz")`) and observed in StepSecurity's published process tree across PIDs 2380/2404/2430/2432. Combined with the seven SHA256 hashes pre-extracted from the article, the detection is hash-anchored — no plausible benign software writes to that path with those hashes. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1105 T1195.002

    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
       or FolderPath has "/tmp/managed.pyz"

    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,

[LLM] GitHub token exfiltration — `gh auth token` / `gh auth status --show-token` spawned by python3 Actions on Objectives High
Detects the credential-access stage of rope.pyz: managed.pyz children running `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` to steal authenticated GitHub PATs from the runner. The python3 parent is the unique pivot — gh CLI normally runs interactively, not as a python child. Rationale: `gh auth token` and `gh auth status --show-token` appear verbatim in the StepSecurity process-tree output across PIDs 2404, 2430, 2432 — each managed.pyz child invokes them independently for redundancy. The python parent constraint eliminates the legit interactive analyst case where gh is launched from a shell. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// rope.pyz credential exfil — gh CLI spawned by python3 to dump GitHub tokens

| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "gh"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("auth token", "auth status --show-token", "auth status -t")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "python"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "python"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentId,
          ProcessId, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// gh token theft via python3 parent — Sentinel ASIM Linux
ImProcessCreate

| where TargetProcessName =~ "gh" or TargetProcessCommandLine startswith "gh "
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("auth token", "auth status --show-token", "auth status -t")
| where ParentProcessName has "python" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "managed.pyz"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="gh" AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python3","python3.14","python") AND (Processes.process="*auth token*" OR Processes.process="*auth status*--show-token*") by host Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

[LLM] Fake pgsql-monitor systemd persistence dropped by python3 Installation High
Detects the persistence stage of rope.pyz — fake systemd user service named pgsql-monitor.service installed by python managed.pyz children, evidenced by `systemctl --user daemon-reload` invocations from the python parent and the service unit file write under ~/.config/systemd/user/. Rationale: The article and process-tree screenshot name `pgsql-monitor.service` explicitly as the persistence artifact and show `systemctl --user daemon-reload` as the activation command across PIDs 2404/2430/2432. The service name was chosen to masquerade as a PostgreSQL monitoring component — but it's installed under the user scope (~/.config/systemd/user/), which is highly unusual for legitimate database monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/actions-security-demo/compromised-packages/actions/runs/26115553485
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
// rope.pyz persistence — pgsql-monitor.service systemd unit + python-triggered daemon-reload
let svcWrite = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service"
       or FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user/pgsql-monitor"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId;
let daemonReload = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName =~ "systemctl"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "--user" and ProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has "python"
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/managed.pyz"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ReportId;
union svcWrite, daemonReload
| order by Timestamp desc
// pgsql-monitor.service systemd persistence (Sentinel ASIM)
let svc = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "pgsql-monitor.service" or TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user/pgsql-monitor"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventProduct;
let reload = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetProcessName =~ "systemctl"
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "--user" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "daemon-reload"
    | where ParentProcessName has "python" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "managed.pyz"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
              TargetProcessCommandLine, EventProduct;
union svc, reload
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: Detects the pgsql-monitor.service systemd user persistence artifact installed by rope.pyz (durabletask supply chain compromise) and the python-driven daemon-reload that activates it.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

status: experimental

    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
